feasibility: The hit must really deal damage and must not be blocked or fully immune (checked inside the class until the librarian adds those conditions)

blocks.packageReason: PACKAGE for the EFFECT only. The trigger (after I am hit) and the resisted-hit condition (two move.effectiveness atoms bound in bindings.ts) are separate and swappable. Why the effect cannot be split with today's blocks: it raises a stat that is chosen by the incoming move's category (physical: one stat, otherwise another) and it updates a private counter and a once-per-foe-move memory; effect.stat-stage has one fixed stat and no memory, so staff would need an effect with a 'stat that matches the hit's category' choice (requested as R-B13-15). The guards (damage dealt, not blocked) and the residual (counter below the cap, new foe move) stay in the class and are listed under 'also requires'; requests R-B13-3, R-B13-4, R-B13-6 and R-B13-14 add the atoms. Review of the numbers: the cap (2), the stages (1) and the two stats (Defense, Sp. Def) were literals; they are now trailing constructor arguments with the old values as defaults and are params. Users: Anneal (5979, attr 1). ODDITIES (not fixed): (1) apply bumps the counter and stores the move record even when simulated (only the stat change is skipped); the harness never simulates PostDefend. (2) The effectiveness gate calls getMoveEffectiveness twice (kept as it was). (3) A resisted move that is 'immune' is excluded by the second clause (effectiveness > 0). (4) The ability text says the raise is for a physical move or a special move; a damaging status-category hit cannot occur, so the 'other' stat only ever follows a special move.

ODDITY (not fixed): apply ignores `simulated`, so a simulated PostSummon call would reset the counter; no engine path simulates PostSummon today.

The trigger (after my hit) is a normal WHEN, the attack condition is the library atom move.damaging (ctor:0) and 'the target was knocked out' is the editable gate (a legacy-closure binding until R-B13-44 `mon.fainted{who}` exists). The 1/8 HP and the 1 stage were literals of that function; they are now constructor arguments 2 and 3 (defaults 8 and 1) and the function reads them from the planter's attr (marker.sourceId -> getPokemonById -> attr; defaults when the planter or attr is gone, so a marker whose planter left the field still behaves as shipped). The base class takes the first two arguments. Users: Boot Hill (5985, attr 0). ODDITIES (not fixed): (1) apply ignores `simulated`, so a simulated call plants a marker; no engine path simulates PostAttack today; (2) the class is also a plain PostAttack effect, so a knock-out by an ordinary hit of a multi-hit move counts on the hit that kills; (3) the marker is planted even when the foe side has no Pokemon left to enter; it is created with 0 turns and is only ever removed by applyGraveMarkerOnEntry; (4) a second marker does not stack, the existing one only changes owner (GraveMarkerTag.onOverlap), so damage credit goes to the latest planter.

The other four clauses are NOT gates a rule could drop: clauses 4 and 5 are the bookkeeping that stops one move use from being counted twice (removing them would make a single move replay itself and corrupt the memory), clause 3 is a correctness rule (R-B13-37, the guard `not-a-scripted-follow-up`) and clause 2 is R-B13-3 (`hit.dealt-damage`). Why the effect cannot be split with today's blocks: it replays the PREVIOUS move of a private per-Pokemon memory (move id, power, type and category) as a scripted follow-up with fixed flags; `effect.scripted-move` takes a fixed move id and power (requested as R-B13-43 `effect.replay-previous-move`, a relative of R-B13-40 `effect.echo-move`). (2) The unleash memory is written by prepareTwoFacedMove and cleared by finishTwoFacedMove in move-effect-phase.ts (found by class name), so the gate depends on engine call sites the declaration cannot show. (3) finishTwoFacedMove clears the face after the move, so the recoil only fires for hits inside the unleashed move itself.

blocks.label: Lower the accuracy of contact moves aimed at me
blocks.summary: Contact moves used against me have their accuracy multiplied by 0.7. Example: 0.7 turns a 100% move into 70%. Moves that never miss are not changed.
examples: Foes' contact moves are 30% more likely to miss me

params.label: Accuracy multiplier (0.7 = 70% of the normal chance)

feasibility: Moves that never miss (accuracy 0 or below) are left alone (checked by the game's accuracy code)
Contact moves that trap the holder (such as Wrap or Fire Spin) also fail to trap it (a fixed rule in the game's trapping check)
